requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The baseline showed appworker absent. The executor then created the account, and direct checks before and after reboot confirmed UID/GID 1000, home /home/appworker, and shell /bin/bash.

requirements.requirement: Give appworker login sessions limits of 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: A root-owned limits configuration sets both soft and hard nofile to 8192 and nproc to 256. Fresh PAM-backed appworker sessions directly reported those effective values before and after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence. The node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, the restart was acknowledged, the post-restart boot ID changed, systemd returned to running, and the account, home, configuration, and effective limits recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the account and limits file was required, and the reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol. The two connection-reset probes were expected during the bounded reboot and show no separate mutation. Afterward, systemd was running, no failed services or package damage were observed, and no unsafe new application listener or abandoned temporary artifact was evident; lifecycle differences are consistent with the reboot.
